item.title: Economics and Strategy Advisory Consultant at AECOM
item.description: At AECOM, we’re delivering a better world.
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
At AECOM, we’re delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world’s trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We’re one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Job Description

AECOM Advisory is seeking a dynamic Economics and Strategy Advisory Consultant to support our growing global Advisory business line. We are seeking talented management consultants to join AECOM Advisory who are mission-driven for the role of our clients in supporting economic, environmental and social vibrancy. We are recruiting for this role in the following metro areas: Boston, MA, New York, NY, Washington DC, Raleigh, NC, Arlington, VA, Philadelphia, PA or Miami, FL.

Join AECOM’s Economics Advisory team to shape decisions on some of the issues that define our lifetime: inclusive growth, climate resilience, the energy transition, and the future of cities, through the real projects AECOM delivers with its clients every day. You will tackle strategic challenges such as translating net-zero ambitions into bankable investment cases, quantifying the socioeconomic value for large-scale investments in energy, water, transportation, and AI infrastructure, and assisting public sector clients in shaping public policy and planning for their key investment and policy priorities.

Building off AECOM’s considerable expertise in infrastructure design and implementation, AECOM Advisory is a trusted adviser to senior level clients and executive teams on their most pressing enterprise and strategic needs.

Our team of 400 staff globally comprises business and policy analysts, economists, commercial strategists, technologists, as well as human capital and change management practitioners. We help our clients develop their strategy, improve their operational performance, and integrate digital systems to generate value for their stakeholders and impact for their communities. We serve the full value chain of clients active in infrastructure, the built environment, and community vibrancy, including: national governments, regulatory entities, city agencies, utilities, transit agencies, infrastructure operators, private corporations, developers and investors. The successful candidate will employ economics methods and rigorous analysis to lead quantitative and qualitative approaches to develop and/or evaluate strategies that address policy, infrastructure investments, supply chain and social challenges.

We are a new category of consulting firm; one that builds off true operational and technical expertise of our broader platform to bring industry depth and capability-driven insight to the clients we serve.

Reporting directly to the Vice President of Economics and Strategy, the consultant will oversee daily operations, manage technical delivery, and help drive the systematic expansion of this strategic service area.

This role demands a blend of expertise in microeconomic analysis, specifically as it pertains to infrastructure, public policy, real estate, and project finance. It also requires consulting skills to offer strategic guidance to public entities, private companies, transportation authorities, and private asset operators and financing partners. The position involves effectively connecting upstream insights to AECOM’s core business lines.

As an Economics and Strategy Advisory Consultant in AECOM Advisory’s US East Region, your day-to-day role will be to define, lead and manage multiple tasks within a workstream as part of a larger engagement.

The responsibilities include but not be limited to:

  • Serve as the principal technical investigator on complex business cases, employing different methods of economic analysis, such as microeconomic modelling, econometric estimations and cost-benefit analyses (CBA), to analyze client problems.

  • Conducting business modelling (market sizing, segmentation, penetration, adoption) and investment analysis by building custom discounted cash flow (DCF) models to calculate revenue, EBITDA, NPV, IRR, CAGR for client’s policies, projects and programs.

  • Leveraging analytical and data visualization tools (e.g., ArcGIS, Costar, IMPLAN, REMI, Python, Tableau) to derive patterns, trends and insights from client and third-party datasets to inform client recommendations. The ability to code your own econometric models is a valuable asset

  • Conducting stakeholder interviews, including with C-suite clients and senior management stakeholders.

  • Outlining, supervising and providing quality control over analytical tasks assigned to junior team members.

  • Creating highly polished executive-ready decks as you work, to build buy-in and convey emerging data-driven insights.

  • Synthesizing multiple inputs into coherent insights across a variety of formats; slide decks, written narrative, playbooks, dashboards and toolkits.

In addition, you will also have the opportunity to contribute to business development, through:

  • Solutions hypothesizing and economic and finance framework development to meet our clients’ needs.

  • Technical writing and long-form narrative development.

  • Creating pitch decks and defining AECOM Advisory’s value proposition.

  • Bringing commercial acumen around client needs, budgetary requirements, researching client contexts.

  • Supporting logistical and administrative processes to ensure risk management and compliance.

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Economics, Public Policy, Finance or quantitatively related degree + 4 years of experience as a professional economist and/or quantitatively inclined management consultant or related experience (e.g., previous roles in business, public policy, economics research, private equity, investment banking or corporate strategy experience); or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education and at least 2 years of Management Consulting or equivalent experience

  • Experience in microeconomic modeling and econometrics, combined with strong numerical reasoning and quantitative business acumen.

  • Experience with funding and financing strategies, including value capture.

  • Experience in economic and fiscal impact analysis.

  • Experience evaluating financial cashflows, particularly public finance.

  • Experience in financial modeling to determine financial feasibility of infrastructure investments

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree in Economics, Public Policy, Finance, quantitatively inclined MBA, and/or related fields. PhD training combined with practical business-oriented experience would be a plus.

  • 8+ years of experience as professional economist and/or quantitatively inclined management consultant.

  • Experience in real estate portfolio optimization and real estate economics is a plus

  • Sharp analytical, logical reasoning and structured problem-solving skills, employing abstraction techniques to solve ambiguous client problems, and ingest and parse out large volumes of client information.

  • Strong commercial insight and willingness to have an informed point-of-view, grounded in an interest in enterprise challenges, its key economic and social rationale and impact, and developing understanding of client industries and their context.

  • Curiosity about infrastructure challenges, our clients, their business, and the industries they operate in.

  • Strong interpersonal skills, client-service mindset and ability to act as a trusted adviser to clients.

  • Work in a high-tempo, high-context client-facing environment, with the ability to maintain poise, maturity and work well under pressure.

  • Able to be self-directed, anticipatory and responsive to iterative feedback.

  • Outstanding attention to detail.

  • Solid verbal communication and narrative development skills, with the ability to summarize and convey key insights to C-suite and senior management audiences.

  • Collegial team-player who can work within a small, motivated team of diverse consulting professionals.

Functional experience in at least one of the following areas desired:

  • Proficiency with data science analytical techniques and familiarity using multiple public datasets including BLS, BEA, NAICS data, ACS and other geographically-defined socioeconomic datasets.

  • Proficiency with geospatial datasets and software e.g., ArcGIS.

  • Proficiency with input-output or general equilibrium economic modelling tools such as Esmi, IMPLAN or REMI.

  • Proficiency with Stata, R, Python and other programming languages.

  • Proficiency with data visualization techniques, such as with PowerBI or Tableau.

Domain expertise in at least one of the following areas desired, but not required:

  • Corporate or enterprise/organizational assessment.

  • Real estate economics and portfolio optimization

  • Project finance and/or infrastructure investment appraisal.

  • Sustainability, climate change, net zero and ESG strategies and frameworks incl. non-financial valuation methodologies.

  • Economic development, industrial policy and market transformation.

Additional Information

THIS POSTING IS FOR A CURRENT VACANCY, AND AECOM INTENDS TO FILL THIS POSITION BY DECEMBER 16, 2026.

  • Sponsorship assistance is not available for this position at this time or in the future.

  • Relocation assistance is not available for this position.

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

About AECOM

AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options, well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.

AECOM is the global infrastructure leader, committed to delivering a better world. As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.

What makes AECOM a great place to work

You will be part of a global team that champions your growth and career ambitions. Work on groundbreaking projects - both in your local community and on a global scale - that are transforming our industry and shaping the future. With cutting-edge technology and a network of experts, you’ll have the resources to make a real impact. Our award-winning training and development programs are designed to expand your technical expertise and leadership skills, helping you build the career you’ve always envisioned. Here, you’ll find a welcoming workplace built on respect, collaboration and community—where you have the freedom to grow in a world of opportunity.

As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in your potential and are here to help you achieve it. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

item.title: Program Evaluation Specialist at American Farmland Trust (remote in US)
item.description: The Program Evaluation Specialist will help lead program impact evaluation efforts at AFT.
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
The Program Evaluation Specialist will help lead program impact evaluation efforts at AFT. The Specialist will help construct and execute this broad and growing effort with objectives to support social science research and advance organizational programs. Specifically, this position will play a strategic role in helping to build larger program impact evaluation efforts across the organization.

Position summary

The Program Evaluation Specialist will help lead the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of program evaluation efforts across AFT. The Specialist will develop evaluation approaches that apply qualitative and quantitative methods to assess program impacts on farmers, ranchers, and agriculture professionals, inform organizational learning, and support evidence-based decision-making for further program refinement and development. The Specialist will work closely with the national research team, regional and national program staff, and other internal teams to collect, analyze, and communicate impact evaluation findings that help advance AFT’s mission. In addition, this highly collaborative position builds upon current efforts to establish broader organizational program evaluation capacity.

Duties and responsibilities

Program Evaluation Leadership

  • Lead the design, implementation, and refinement of new program evaluation frameworks across AFT initiatives.

  • Develop evaluation plans aligned with program objectives.

  • Establish standardized evaluation approaches that can be applied across multiple programs while accommodating program-specific needs.

  • Identify opportunities to expand and improve organizational evaluation capacity.

Data Collection and Analysis

  • Design and implement qualitative and quantitative data collection methods, including surveys, interviews, focus groups, and other evaluation tools informed by organizational needs and peer-reviewed literature.

  • Manage data collection activities to ensure data quality, consistency, and confidentiality.

  • Support development of an internal database and data management system.

  • Synthesize findings into meaningful conclusions that support program improvement and organizational learning.

Reporting and Communication

  • Prepare technical reports, summaries, presentations, and other communication products that clearly convey evaluation findings to internal and external audiences.

  • Translate evaluation results into practical recommendations for program staff, leadership, funders, and partners.

  • Contribute evaluation findings to grant reports, publications, presentations, and other organizational communications as appropriate.

Collaboration and Technical Support

  • Lead a collaborative effort to create an organization-wide impact evaluation system and toolkit for all staff.

  • Collaborate with program staff and external partners throughout the evaluation process.

  • Provide technical assistance to program teams on evaluation design, data collection, and interpretation of results.

  • Facilitate workshops, meetings, and stakeholder discussions to support evaluation planning and dissemination of findings.

  • Foster collaborative relationships that strengthen organizational learning.

Research and Organizational Learning

  • Identify and implement emerging evaluation methods, tools, and best practices relevant to AFT programs.

  • Contribute to applied social science research that advances understanding of program effectiveness and participant outcomes.

  • Support the integration of evaluation findings into program planning, strategic decision-making, and organizational learning initiatives.

This is not necessarily an all-inclusive list of job-related responsibilities. Management reserves the right to revise the job or to require other or different duties be performed as assigned.

Qualifications

  • MS degree in a social science-related discipline preferred or a related BS degree

  • Documented 2-5 years of professional experience conducting program evaluation

  • Preferred background in agriculture, ecosystem services, environmental science, or a similar field

  • Documented experience working with both qualitative and quantitative data

    • Survey experience using software such as Survey Monkey or Qualtrics

    • Managing confidential data and protecting respondent identities with data management systems

    • Analyzing quantitative data using software such as Excel or R

    • Analyzing qualitative data using software such as NVivo or Dedoose

  • Collaborative and constructive team member

  • Self-starter with ability to work independently

  • Group facilitation experience

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex data into language accessible to multiple audiences (researchers, program staff, farmers and ranchers, etc.)

  • Committed to AFT’s mission of protecting farmland, promoting sound practices, and helping to keep farmers on the land

Working conditions

This job operates primarily in a teleworking environment during normal business hours in a local US time zone. Occasional work in the evenings or on weekends may be required to meet deadlines.

Some travel may be required to meet project deliverables. This may include conducting in-person workshops, focus groups, or surveys, among other project-related tasks and activities.

Degree of Supervision Received

General Supervision: The incumbent normally receives minimal instruction on day-to-day work and receives general instructions on new assignments.

Degree of Supervision Given

This position reports to the Senior Social Scientist (Social Science Focus Area Lead) and will work collaboratively internally and externally as part of AFT’s Research division.

Compensation
American Farmland Trust offers excellent vacation, medical, retirement and other benefits. The salary range for this position is from $70,000 to $80,000 based upon experience.

American Farmland Trust offers a full benefits package for full time employees:

  • Insurance coverage begins the 1st of the month following the date of hire.

  • Medical & Prescription Coverage

  • Dental Coverage

  • Vision Coverage

  • Company Paid Life Insurance & Long-Term Disability (LTD)

  • Voluntary Life Insurance

  • Flexible Spending Account (FSA) – Healthcare & Dependent Care

  • Health Savings Account (HSA)

  • 401k Plan

  • Sick Leave: Regular full-time employees accrue 13 “sick days” per year.

  • Vacation Leave: Accrue 15 days during the first year increasing by one day per year to 20 days per year maximum.

  • Holidays: AFT observes twelve fixed holidays and a week between Christmas and New Years off during the year (all offices closed) plus a choice of up to three (depending on hiring month) floating holidays.

Why you should apply

  • Be a part of a purpose-driven, committed, knowledgeable, high-performing, experienced and fun team

  • A diverse and inclusive work environment

  • A cause and mission you can be proud of

  • Competitive compensation & benefits

  • Remote work opportunity

Timeline

To be considered applicants must submit a resume, answer all screener questions and include a cover letter explaining what they are a right fit for both AFT and this role. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the role is filled.

Please apply directly through AFT’s Paycom Career Portal using this link: Program Evaluation Specialist

If the link is unavailable, please visit AFT’s Careers page and select this position to submit your application.

item.title: Director of Programs at ACDI/VOCA (remote in US)
item.description: ACDI/VOCA is a global non-profit development design and delivery partner based in Washington DC.
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
ACDI/VOCA is a global non-profit development design and delivery partner based in Washington DC. We have implemented effective economic and social development programs around the world since 1963. We address issues of food security, economic prosperity, and social engagement by facilitating the creation of durable, locally driven market, food, and social systems in communities around the world.

ACDI/VOCA is a member of AV Group, together with its affiliate organizations Tanager, AV Ventures, and Frontiers. We are a family of global development organizations that work together and individually to achieve our shared mission: improving the lives of families and the health of communities worldwide.

POSITION SUMMARY

As part of the Programs team, the Director, Programs will be responsible for overall project management including technical, financial, and operational oversight, playing a key role in advancing AV Group’s global impact. Duties include liaising with other departments and affiliate organizations, providing technical and operational guidance to projects, ensuring compliance with ACDI/VOCA and client policies and regulations, identifying and leading new business pursuits, and supporting the larger Programs department. The ideal candidate is a team leader who exercises sound judgement, a relationship builder who thrives in a fast-paced collaborative environment and prioritizes work appropriately, and a problem solver eager to strengthen the systems, relationships, and field operations that make development work possible. The candidate must have professional proficiency in Spanish to enable effective written and verbal communication with project teams and stakeholders. Directors are expected to manage projects with minimal guidance and input. Reporting to the Department Head, this role offers an opportunity to contribute meaningfully to mission-driven work while building leadership experience across project and proposal management.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES:

Project and Client Management

  • Establish positive and interactive relationships with project donors and partner organizations; understand donor/partner priorities and goals and ensure the project addresses them.

  • Work with project field teams to facilitate creation of work plans using ACDI/VOCA standardized approaches and tools. Establish submission timelines and identify relevant resources for support. Ensure work plans are directly related to project deliverables, responsive to the donor, and meet ACDI/VOCA standards.

  • Conduct routine work plan progress evaluations and ensure work occurring is in line with work plan design and on schedule. Help problem solve/enhance as needed.

  • Engage and coordinate with MEL specialists/consultants to ensure projects are supported in implementing MEL Plans. Ensure baseline, mid-term, and annual surveys/evaluations are implemented on time and in accordance with the agreement/contract.

  • Review, provide feedback, and approve quarterly, annual progress, and other project reports for submission to the donor ensuring they meet ACDI/VOCA quality standards and are on time.

  • Ensure timely development and submission of Environmental Assessments and/or Management Plans, Safeguarding, and other donor due diligence requirements.

  • Ensure grant fund usage aligns with programmatic objectives. Review grant packages for technical components and ensure deliverables align with expected results.

  • Liaise with COP/Team Lead to ensure sub-awardees’ technical performance meets expectations and acceptable deliverables are submitted

  • Engage and coordinate with technical specialists/consultants to ensure technical and learning support is provided, and results/successes are shared within ACDI/VOCA (including lessons learned), as well as the broader international development community as appropriate.

  • Lead recruitment efforts for STTA, consultants, and project staff as necessary.

  • Ensure projects are using ACDI/VOCA standard project management tools.

  • As needed, independently deliver specific technical assistance as STTA to projects.

  • Participate in appropriate professional organizations; stay current on major themes in the profession; establish an external professional network.

Operational

  • Monitor start-up of new projects, follow progress through start-up action plan trackers, ensure timely execution, and support and problem solve as needed.

  • Monitor procurement and compliance within ACDI/VOCA and donor policies and procedures and ensure that projects have procurement plans.

  • Lead recruitment efforts for key personnel, draft key personnel requests and submit requests to donors.

  • Monitor grant fund compliance and spending. Ensure projects have a grant management manual.

  • Work with COPs to finalize SOWs with sub-awardees; and develop sub-awardees management plans with COPs.

  • Ensure sub-awards w/local and international partners are signed on time, monitored, and reviewed properly. Review, approve, and submit deliverables/invoices in accordance with agreements and increase obligations accordingly.

  • Ensure projects have updated security and contingency plans with COP/Team Lead. Ensure timely submission of quarterly vehicle report; ensure projects report all vehicle accidents within 24 hours; and ensure projects have an updated property management registry.

  • Identify and flag implementation and financial risks; draft risk authorization letters for approval as needed.

  • Ensure timely project close out in accordance with ACDI/VOCA policies and procedures in conjunction with COPs/Team Leads and project teams.

Financial

  • Review monthly project financial and budget reports (JSRs) for variances and discuss issues with COPs/Team Leads and Department Head as needed.

  • Review outstanding advances and ensure that they are liquidated promptly (no later than 90 days).

  • Analyze and review project budgets including projections and actuals (ETCs); identify issues and discuss with the COPs/Team Leads to ensure they are resolved.

  • Ensure routine budget meetings take place, incorporating financial analysis and operational updates from the project team.

  • Monitor obligation and request additional obligated funds at a 70 percent threshold, when applicable.

  • Prepare/contribute to budget realignments and submit for donor approval if required.

  • Review and approve deliverables for STTA/consulting assignments and approve payment.

  • Review project invoices as applicable and review all financial reports prior to submission to the donor.

New Business Development

  • Contribute to proposal efforts as Proposal Leader, Technical Writer or another key role for the AV Group (ACDI/VOCA, Tanager, AV Ventures).

  • Independently identify and qualify new business opportunities in collaboration with the Department Head and business development team to achieve new business goals.

  • Conduct regular calls and meetings with diverse donors, clients, and partners, including government, foundation, corporate, and institutional funders, to explore new business opportunities and position AV Group as a preferred partner.

  • Track country specific donor opportunities and project add-ons; identify strategies to capture these opportunities and work with the Department Head to allocate resources to opportunities.

  • Lead proposal activities to ensure competitive and compliant submissions; activities may span the full proposal cycle and include identifying partner organizations, leading teaming discussions, leading in-country capture trips, conducting primary and secondary research, leading proposal design, writing or reviewing proposal sections, interviewing and identifying key personnel, developing and reviewing budgets.

Additional Duties

  • Represent AV Group at conferences, industry events, and other venues.

  • Supervise, train and develop Project Specialists/Managers in completing routine day-today administrative, financial and operational activities; guide Project Specialists/Managers to resolve complex or difficult issues; and demonstrate extensive understanding of administrative and financial regulations and policies.

  • Oversee COPs/Team Leads and/or Component Leads for designated projects.

  • Instill, strengthen, and promote a culture of professionalism, collaboration, and inclusion within the organization, demonstrating behaviors that staff will emulate.

QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS:

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required; reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • Master’s degree in international development, economics, business, or another related field required. Equivalent combination of education and work experience in the relevant technical area may be substituted for master’s degree.

  • Minimum 7 years of experience, plus 2 years of managerial experience, including overseas work, in international development or related field required.

  • Demonstrated experience and technical knowledge in economic development required.

  • Experience in backstopping USG and non-USG funded programs required.

  • Excellent analytical and technical skills and expertise with the ability to work independently.

  • Experience with Microsoft Office, Sharepoint, ERP and CRM systems.

  • Strong interpersonal and team skills, with ability to work with individuals from diverse backgrounds and cultures.

  • Fluency in English required. Professional proficiency in Spanish required.

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills required.

  • Ability and willingness to travel internationally required; may be required to be vaccinated based on country requirements.

LOCATION

This position will be fully remote.

SALARY RANGE

The salary range for this position is $93,000 to $121,000; candidate’s relevant experience and skills, as well as our internal equity, will be considered before an offer is extended.

APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS

Please apply by October 9, 2026, by emailing your resume and cover letter to Programs@joinav.org. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

ACDI/VOCA IS AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

item.title: (Senior) Consultant at Energy + Environmental Economics (US or Canada)
item.description: When you join the E3 team, you will be working on some of the most important energy issues with some of the top minds in the electricity industry.
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
When you join the E3 team, you will be working on some of the most important energy issues with some of the top minds in the electricity industry. We help shape energy and climate policy, play vital roles in regulatory proceedings, advise executives, and inform investment and planning selections. At E3, you will be challenged and inspired.

Who We Are

Founded in 1989, Energy + Environmental Economics (E3) is a fast-growing energy consulting firm that helps utilities, regulators, policy makers, developers, and investors make the most educated strategic decisions possible as they implement new public policies, deploy and develop new technologies, and address customers’ shifting expectations. We have offices in San Francisco, New York City, Boston, Denver, and Calgary.

Because E3 works with customers from all sectors of the electricity industry, we provide a 360-degree knowledge of markets, planning, policy, regulation, and environmental factors. Just as important, we are driven to deliver clear, unbiased evaluations that help customers make informed decisions.

E3 works on high-profile, high-impact projects in jurisdictions that spearhead the implementation of clean energy policy. In California, Hawaii, and New York, we are advising state agencies and regulators about how to implement clean energy policies with an emphasis on customer incentives and markets.

About You

We look for people who combine strong analytical dexterity and/or policy experience with integrity and a passion for energy. Our Consultants love to examine, research, and offer creative solutions to some of the most elaborate and important energy issues of the day. You bring curiosity, thrive in a rigorous and quantitative solution-finding environment, take a proactive approach to assist the team, and are practiced at clearly presenting information to a variety of stakeholders. We seek those that are inquisitive and look at all sides of an issue to make informed recommendations with confidence and clarity. You pride yourself in your attention to detail and your organizational techniques help you create and actualize work plans that are efficient while delivering an elevated level of guidance to serve our customers.

The Work

The Consultant is a vital contributor to our team and project work. The position assists and/or spearheads client-facing interactions and plays an engaged role in identifying the approach and methods for project tasks. Our consultants direct workstreams within projects and contribute heavily to written reports and papers. Our consultants have the opportunity to deliver findings and summaries to customers, make presentations, and reply to questions. Duties will grow to include more elaborate investigative tasks, core QA/QC of products, and becoming a technical head on various project needs and/or a flagship modeling tool.

Work Environment

Hybrid and flexible work environment that adapts to changing needs of projects. E3 thrives in a strong collaborative office-based working environment but has also adapted to the safety requirements of our employees. Must be able to work for extended hours in front of a computer screen and conduct meetings on the telephone and virtually.

General

- Hours: Full Time

- Type: Exempt

- Travel: 0-5%

- Office Location: San Francisco, Boston, New York, or Calgary

Typical Responsibilities

  • Assist the delivery of customer work through modeling, developing presentations, writing and preparing entire subsections of reports and papers, and helping with additional customer requests

  • Conduct independent research using your ingenuity and curiosity to make reasonable assumptions and produce appropriate solutions, at times with incomplete information.

  • Fulfill end-to-end internal project obligations

  • Deliver sections of presentations to customers and reply to questions

  • Tackles elaborate analytical tasks

  • Apply core QA/QC best practices

  • Develop aptitude in using a flagship modeling tool, gathering relevant data, and vetting results

  • Assist in proposal writing as needed

  • Translate results of research and evaluations into clear visual representations

  • Aid project heads in the creation or editing of spreadsheets to be “client-ready,” including developing tools for customer solutions

  • Make modifications to existing tools and models to improve functionality and/or efficiency

  • Proactively track actual performance of own work performed against the established plan, with ongoing communication with the Director or Manager

  • Capture project learnings and repeatable products and work samples for future use according to knowledge management processes

  • Assist with internal initiatives as needed

Requirements

  • Master’s degree or PhD in engineering, economics, computer science, public policy, or related field

  • 3-5+ years of related experience in an energy-related field

  • Prior experience specifically addressing renewable energy and climate change issues and/or demonstrated advanced-level academic related project work

  • Demonstrated hands-on experience, academic project work, or extensive knowledge in or related to one of our Practice Areas: Energy Planning and Policy (EPP), Transmission, Pricing, and Risk (TPR), Market Advisory and Valuation (MAV), and Distribution Technology and Planning (DTP)

  • You work collaboratively and help each member of your team to do their finest work, aware that each brings different experiences to the table

  • You find joy in translating technical concepts to broader audiences

  • You take ownership of your work, proactively seeking out answers to questions and enjoy finding creative solutions to issues you encounter

  • Aptitude to write and communicate clearly

  • Passionate about the transition to a low-carbon economy

  • Demonstrated success guiding ideas, people, and projects

  • Strong organizational and time management techniques

  • High fluency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint; programming knowledge and experience are also valued

  • Desire to work in a dynamic office environment with staff

Things that Set You Apart

  • Meaningful project management experience

  • You believe it is essential to achieve a transition to a low-carbon economy and love thinking about the future of energy

$115,000 - $150,000 a year

Compensation and Title

E3 takes a number of factors into consideration when determining salary level for a potential new employee. This includes, but is not limited to: a candidate’s education, training, and relevant work experience; expected quality and quantity of work; required travel (if any); external market and internal value, including seniority and merit systems; and internal pay alignment.​

​

E3 also provides a bonus structure that we are proud of because we believe it creates the right kinds of incentives for good work, provides significant flexibility, and is fair and equitable. The below compensation outlines our total compensation package with our bonus structure adding between 15 - 25% to your base salary. item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
This position is located in the USDA, Office of the Chief Economist (OCE) which is responsible for conducting advanced economic analysis and analyzing policy options related to complex domestic and global agricultural issues. The position requires recognized expertise in agricultural economics and substantial experience analyzing policy and legislative options for complex issues, particularly related to agricultural input markets, international agricultural trade, and/or biofuel markets.

This job is open to

The public

U.S. Citizens, Nationals or those who owe allegiance to the U.S.

Career transition (CTAP, ICTAP, RPL)

Federal employees whose job, agency or department was eliminated and are eligible for priority over other applicants.

Clarification from the agency

Applications will be accepted from any U.S. citizen. Direct Hire Authority will be used to fill this position. Veterans Preference and traditional rating and ranking of applicants does not apply to this vacancy.

Duties

  • Serves as a senior agricultural economist and recognized expert in the economic analysis of policy options of complex issues, specializing in agricultural input markets, international agricultural trade, and/or biofuel markets.

  • Develops and recommends appropriate research methods and analytical techniques to analyze the economic impact of relevant policy options.

  • Applies mastery of economic theory, quantitative methods, econometrics, and interdisciplinary analytical techniques to resolve difficult problems of substantial importance to USDA.

  • Designs, conducts, and presents sophisticated economic research and multi-disciplinary analyses that inform OCE leadership, USDA agencies, and interagency partners.

  • Compares the likely economic impact of alternative proposals; independently plans and executes assigned analyses.

  • Supports the Chief/Deputy Chief Economist by framing analytical options in areas where significant differences of opinion or political sensitivities exist.

  • Provides advice so interpretations and recommendations can be grounded in rigorous economic analysis, and provides guidance on data and statistical issues involved in analysis of agricultural policy, input markets, trade, biofuels, and/or production.

  • Exercises substantial responsibility in shaping analytical approaches and ensuring alignment with OCE priorities.

  • Collaborates with senior staff across USDA agencies, represents OCE in interagency working groups, and maintains professional relationships with universities, industry groups, and stakeholders.

  • Analyzes and evaluates legislative proposals that cut across agriculture and trade areas for policy and program implications.

  • Prepares briefings, speeches, and reports explaining economic and policy implications of key issues for internal leadership, interagency partners, Congressional audiences, and external stakeholders; contributes expert perspectives.

  • Communicates clearly, both orally and in writing, to convey complex technical results for use by both technical and nontechnical personnel.

  • Reviews, consolidates, and synthesizes economic and statistical analyses across agency lines.

  • Responsible for adequacy of data, analytical methods and reliability of results.

  • Responsible for the interpretation, coordination, and technical application of research and analysis.

Requirements

Conditions of employment

  • You must be a US Citizen or US National.

  • Males born after 12/31/1959 must be Selective Service registered or exempt.

  • Subject to satisfactory adjudication of background investigation and/or fingerprint check.

  • If selected, you may be required to serve a probationary or trial period as applicable to appointment type.

  • Direct Deposit: Per Public Law 104-134 all Federal employees are required to have federal payments made by direct deposit to their financial institution.

  • Successfully pass the E-Verify employment verification check. To learn more about E-Verify, including your rights and responsibilities, visit E-Verify at https://www.e-verify.gov/.

Qualifications

Applicants must meet all qualifications and eligibility requirements by the closing date of the announcement including Basic Requirements and Minimum Qualification Requirements, as defined below.

Basic Requirements:

In addition to meeting the Minimum Qualification Requirements outlined in the following section, applicants MUST meet the following occupational series requirements:

A. Economist Series, 0110

Degree: economics, that included at least 21 semester hours in economics and 3 semester hours in statistics, accounting, or calculus.

OR

Combination of education and experience: courses equivalent to a major in economics, as shown above, plus appropriate experience or additional education.

Minimum Qualification Requirements: In addition to meeting at least one of the Basic Requirements outlined above, applicants must also meet the specialized experience and/or education requirements shown below. If qualifying based on experience, your application or resume must clearly show that you possess the specialized experience requirements.

Time in grade:

Current federal employees applying for a promotion opportunity must meet time-in-grade (TIG) requirement of 52 weeks of service at the next lower grade level in the normal line of progression for the position being filled.

Specialized Experience:

GS-14: One year of specialized experience, equivalent to the GS-13 level in the Federal service or equivalent responsibility in the private sector/pay systems that has equipped the candidate with the particular competencies to successfully perform as a Senior Agricultural Economist. The specialized experience is having the knowledge, skills and abilities to perform the duties of the position described as experience (1) mastery of economic theory, quantitative methods, econometrics, and interdisciplinary analytical techniques to analyze the economic impact of policy options affecting domestic and foreign agricultural policy, commodity input markets, trade, biofuel markets, and production; (2) experience providing authoritative advice in developing, implementing and disseminating those analyses; and (3) a demonstrated ability to communicate economic findings and concepts to non-technical audiences.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Education

All applicants must meet at least one of the Basic Requirements as outlined in the above Qualifications section.

item.title: Economic Analyst at The Dakota Institute
item.description: The Dakota Institute conducts independent economic research and advisory work for organizations throughout South Dakota and the Northern Plains.
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
The Dakota Institute conducts independent economic research and advisory work for organizations throughout South Dakota and the Northern Plains. Our engagements include statewide economic impact studies, fiscal feasibility analysis for municipalities and development projects, and research and consulting services for foundations, public institutions, and industry organizations.

As an analyst, you’ll work on projects from end-to-end — from initial data collection to the final deliverable — working closely with leadership and directly with the clients who use the work. The scope of the role is unusually wide for an analyst position.

We’re looking for someone with a strong technical background, the judgment to structure an analysis independently, and the ability to communicate findings clearly to technical and non-technical audiences alike.

Objectives and Responsibilities

  • Analyze economic data to identify trends and opportunities relevant to policymakers, business leaders, and clients.

  • Write research reports, including data tables and visualizations, that clients and stakeholders use to make decisions.

  • Build and maintain the workflows and processes behind our data collection, analysis, and reporting.

  • Develop and maintain public dashboards tracking economic conditions in the state and region.

  • Collect and update various datasets on a regular basis.

Required skills and qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree (or higher), preferably in economics, data science, computer science, mathematics, or business.

  • Advanced analytical skills with experience collecting, cleaning, and analyzing complex data using appropriate software tools.

  • Exceptional verbal and written communication skills.

Preferred skills and qualifications

  • Two or more years’ experience in applied data analysis and research writing.

  • Proficiency with data analysis tools such as R (preferred), Python, or Stata.

  • Experience with economic impact modeling software such as REMI and IMPLAN.

  • Experience developing data visualizations using software such as R, Python, Tableau, or Power BI.

  • Familiarity with South Dakota’s economy, key industries, and policy environment.

Job Type & Location

  • Full-time, based in our Sioux Falls office.

  • Flexible scheduling.

Pay & Benefits

  • $60,000 to $80,000 based on qualifications.

  • Paid time off from day 1.

  • SIMPLE IRA retirement benefit and Health benefit stipend (ICHRA) from day 1.

How to Apply

  • Apply through the LinkedIn page.

  • Send a copy of your resume and a cover letter to info@dakotainstitute.org

  • Use the subject line “Dakota Institute Economic Analyst”.

  • You may be asked to provide a brief writing sample (a research summary, policy memo, or similar analytical piece) after applying.

item.title: Dean of College of Agriculture and Life Sciences at Iowa State University
item.description: Iowa State University (ISU) is a very special place and full of history.
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
Iowa State University (ISU) is a very special place and full of history. But what truly makes Iowa State unique is a rare combination of campus beauty, the opportunity to be a part of the land-grant mission, and the progressive and inventive spirit of the Cyclone experience.

The first class graduated in 1872. Iowa State established the nation’s first state veterinary medicine school in 1879. In 1959, the college was officially renamed Iowa State University of Science and Technology.

In addition to being classified as a Carnegie Foundation Doctoral/Research University – Extensive, Iowa State is ranked by U.S. News and World Report as one of the top public universities in the nation. Over 31,000 students are enrolled and are served by over 6,200 faculty and staff. Committed to its land-grant mission, the University is organized into eight colleges, including the Graduate College. The University provides a broad array of academic degree programs, including more than 100 bachelor’s degree programs, one Professional degree, over 100 master’s programs, over 80 Ph.D. programs, and over 60 certificate programs. In FY 25, Iowa State secured $329.9 million in external research funding. The College of Agriculture and Life Sciences (CALS) was founded in 1858 and is the birthplace of the modern extension system.

The University’s strategic plan is based upon four pillars: innovative solutions, education experience, community engagement, and knowledge & discovery. Intersected and interwoven throughout the pillars are its land-grant university hallmarks of teaching, research, service, and extension. Most importantly, the pillars give structure and direction on how the university will make a difference for its state and world in the years ahead.

Our Mission: Iowa State University will create, share, and apply knowledge to make our students, Iowa, and the world better.

Our Vision: Iowa State University will advance the land-grant ideals of putting science, technology, and human creativity to work.

Our Values: Iowa State University embraces the values of our Principles of Community (Respect, Purpose, Cooperation, Richness of Diversity, Freedom from Discrimination, Honest and Respectful Expression of Ideas) and the values of Access, Excellence, and Integrity.

Academics

More opportunities. More possibilities. More potential. With more than 100 majors to choose from, undergraduate students can customize their academic journey to maximize their impact in the world. From the first step on campus, they will be surrounded by world-renowned professors, resume-building opportunities, and state-of-the-art facilities.

Iowa State University offers graduate study in more than 180 graduate programs. Choose a full or part-time master’s or doctoral degree, a campus-based or online master’s degree, or even a certificate. For those who need to enhance credentials with additional coursework, or are simply interested in taking a class or two, a non-degree-seeking option can be considered. Students can discover and learn within small groups of peers and faculty in classes, seminars, labs, studios, and internship opportunities.

ISU Campus and Ames, IA

Fun things to do and endless places to visit. Unique shops and delicious dining. Concerts and performances featuring renowned and up-and-coming names.

Iowa State University and the city of Ames offer a perfect blend of arts, culture and entertainment with a stunning backdrop no matter the season – spring, summer, fall, and winter. Whether you’re exploring campus or the Ames community, beauty and wonder are around every corner.

Ames, Iowa is a growing community of 65,000, located approximately 30 minutes north of Des Moines. Ames has 35 parks, 55 miles of bike and pedestrian trails, golf courses, lakes, and an aquatics center for outdoor recreation. Anchored by the beautiful Iowa State Campus and with a low cost of living, Ames is a great place to live, work, and raise a family.

University Museums encompasses two art museums, a National Historic Landmark historic home museum, a sculpture garden, and one of the largest campus public art collections in the nation.

From the Wall Street Journal to Forbes Magazine, the city of Ames continually ranks among America’s best cities to live, work, study, and play.

About the College of Agriculture and Life Sciences

The College of Agriculture and Life Sciences is one of the world’s leading institutions of agriculture, with more than 160 years of leadership in science, education and extension. The college educates future leaders, conducts mission-oriented research and shares new knowledge for the betterment of Iowa and the world. The college is one of eight colleges at Iowa State University, which is one of the most influential land grant universities in the nation. CALS at ISU is a comprehensive agricultural college, offering degrees and research programs in just about every aspect in the agricultural and rural space.

Iowa is a national and global leader in agriculture, with recognized strengths in food and renewable fuel production and a deep commitment to responsible resource stewardship. Across the state, influential leaders from agriculture, food, energy, conservation, and agribusiness—from small enterprises to major organizations—engage with our students, staff, and faculty.

The College of Agriculture and Life Sciences offers 28 undergraduate majors and 35 graduate programs in addition to hands-on opportunities for students to hone skills in leadership, communications and technical skills, within and across disciplines.

  • The college hosts the nation’s largest career fair and employers compete for its graduates: placement has been 97 percent or higher for 26 consecutive years.

  • Approximately $4 million in scholarships are offered to students annually through the college and its departments.

  • The college leads the campus in first-year retention rates and has the highest four-year graduation rate.

  • Iowa State’s agricultural and biosystems engineering programs consistently rank amongst the top programs nationwide, according to U.S. News & World Report.

  • CALS students interested in entrepreneurship can become involved in the Start Something College of Agriculture and Life Sciences program.

  • CALS manages 15 different research farms throughout the state, with more than 130 Iowa State faculty using the farms for various projects. In addition, 2,000 students receive hands-on learning experiences at the farms each year.

Agriculture and Natural Resources Extension Program

The Agriculture and Natural Resources (ANR) Extension program serves Iowans daily, delivering science-based information and education vital to farmers, businesses, communities and consumers. ANR engages with stakeholders to better understand needs, anticipate emerging issues, and inform future planning efforts. ANR is the largest unit in ISU Extension and Outreach, involving 84 faculty and staff in eight departments and 39 field specialists across Iowa. The ANR Extension network of campus-based state specialists and field specialists include natural resources, agricultural engineering, commercial horticulture, farm management, agronomists, agronomy, and livestock production beef specialists, swine specialists, and dairy specialists.

Advancing Science and Agriculture

The College of Agriculture and Life Sciences at Iowa State University drives research and discovery through its Iowa Agriculture and Home Economics Experiment Station, building on 130+ years of national and international research leadership. CALS researchers span fields from agriculture, life sciences and social sciences, applying basic and applied science to tackle real-world problems. The Experiment Station’s collaborative model supports research within CALS and across other Iowa State colleges and units, as well as with partners globally to fulfill the land-grant mission of improving agriculture and communities.

The college is also a powerhouse in attracting competitive grants – it ranks in the top seven U.S. agricultural colleges for faculty with federal research grants and in the top ten for the total number of federal grants (2025 Academic Analytics). Over the last five years, CALS Experiment Station scientists have secured over $249 million (over $49 million annually) in external research funding (February 2025), fueling investigations that expand scientific frontiers. This strong funding base is diversified across federal agencies, industry, state and commodity groups, reflecting broad support for CALS research endeavors.

Global Recognition and Impact

CALS research programs rank among the best in the world. In the 2025 QS World University Rankings, Iowa State’s agriculture and forestry programs were rated No. 12 globally (top 4% of 477 institutions) and No. 6 in the U.S. CALS operates global partnerships and international programs through its Office for Global Engagement, which has active research and development activities in over 40 countries.

$4 mil. in scholarships are offered to students annually

98% of graduates reported they were working, continuing their education or serving in the military within six months of graduating

4% CALS ranks among the top 4% worldwide among other agriculture and forestry programs

$249M in external research funding over last five years

Top 7 U.S. agricultural colleges for faculty with federal research grants

The Role

Iowa State University, one of the nation’s leading land-grant institutions, seeks nominations and applications for the position of Dean of the College of Agriculture and Life Sciences and Director of the Iowa Agricultural and Home Economics Experiment Station. Iowa State seeks a proven leader who can build upon the College’s strengths in plant and animal sciences, food and human nutrition, agricultural and biosystems engineering, social sciences, life sciences, and natural resources management in Iowa and throughout the world. Given these strengths, the Dean should effectively promote and champion the College to internal and external stakeholders, exhibit a passion for the convergent disciplines that fuel its success, and create a clear, strategic vision for advancing its research, teaching, and extension activities. Apart from the significant amount of unrestricted funds to use at the Dean’s discretion, the successful candidate will hold the Endowed Deanship, a $4 million endowment of which the proceeds are used solely to support the Dean’s priorities for the college. For more information about the College, visit www.cals.iastate.edu.

CALS faculty and their corresponding research programs are among the most highly cited in the world. CALS is comprised of 14 academic departments (8 jointly administered with another College) and 26 centers and institutes. Reporting to the university’s Senior Vice President and Provost, the Dean provides forward-looking planning for the education of approximately 3,500 undergraduates and 550 graduate students. The College has a budget for teaching, research, and extension that exceeds $106 million.

The selected candidate must possess an earned doctoral degree and have a distinguished record that qualifies the candidate for tenure at the rank of full professor in one of the College’s departments. They must also have:

  • A vision for the teaching, research and outreach missions of a premier land-grant university;

  • Demonstrated achievement working with individuals and stakeholder groups locally, nationally, and internationally, including commodity groups, to advance organizational priorities and strengthen partnerships;

  • Leadership experience in a complex academic, governmental, or business organization;

  • A passion for improving agriculture and rural communities in Iowa;

  • The ability to build and sustain internal and external collaborations; and

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills;

Preferred qualifications include extensive experience in private fund raising and securing philanthropic gifts to support student scholarships, academic programs, facilities, and research.

How to Apply

The Search Committee invites nominations, expressions of interest, or applications (a letter of interest, comprehensive curriculum vitae, and contact information of five or more references) which may be submitted in confidence to the Buffkin/Baker search firm:

Martin M. Baker, Managing Partner, Buffkin/Baker martin@buffkinbaker.com

Applications will be accepted until the position is filled. However, to receive full consideration, it is preferred that applications be submitted by October 5, 2026.

item.title: Chief of Party for Regrow Yirga Coffee Program at TechnoServe (Ethiopia)
item.description: Everyone deserves the opportunity to build a better future.
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
Everyone deserves the opportunity to build a better future. This simple idea has been at the heart of TechnoServe’s work around the world for over 50 years. TechnoServe is a pioneer in leveraging the power of business and markets to create sustainable pathways out of poverty.

The low-income communities in which we work are full of enterprising people. Their small-scale farms and businesses are the keys to economic development. But they face many challenges: low literacy, lack of access to jobs and markets, unpredictable political dynamics and, increasingly, the effects of climate change. For many women and young people, the challenges are even more daunting. Working with TechnoServe staff, people around the world are lifting themselves out of poverty. The results are amazing...when incomes increase and living conditions for families get better, they are able to access health care and education previously out of reach. Communities and even whole countries are better off.

About the project:

TechnoServe seeks a results-oriented professional to manage the implementation of one of TechnoServe’s largest programs in Africa. The coffee project is focused reviving the coffee sector in Yirgacheffe; one of the world’s most celebrated coffee origins. The program helps farmers boost productivity and expand trade and has a strong focus on improving farmers´ capacity to renew their trees. Specifically, the Regrow Yirga program seeks to: train 42,000 farmers in good agricultural practices, provide quality advisory support to 45 coffee processing stations, and work with a research institute and government to improve the climate-resilient capacity of coffee varietals and strengthen private coffee service providers in Ethiopia. Lastly, the project will launch an innovative Farmer Stumping Fund which will facilitate direct incentive (tools or cash) transfers to farmers to encourage tree rejuvenation which has the potential to be scaled up to over 1 million coffee farmers nation-wide.

The project works together with stakeholders at each stage of the supply chain including farmers, processors, exporters, roasting companies, industry associations, (private) service providers and government institutions. The primary goal of the project is income creation for smallholder farmers, while environmental sustainability, gender equity, job creation and increased trade are important secondary goals.

This program is in its implementation phase, and is funded through March 2028. The selected candidate’s offer is contingent upon donor approval.

Primary Functions & Responsibilities:

The Chief of Party (COP) will lead overall management of program operations and ensure effective and timely project implementation as well as high quality service delivery to clients and achieving an optimal return on invested funds. The COP will be responsible for:

  • Providing overall strategic guidance, leadership, management, and general technical oversight of the entire project, with a strong focus on achieving defined key performance indicators.

  • Acting as the key liaison with all counterparts, implementing partners, and stakeholders involved with the project.

  • Acting as the spokesperson for the project and presenting its work regionally and globally

  • Recruiting, leading, and supervising delivery teams compromising long- and short-term team members and consortium partners (~150 staff). Establish a positive and harassment free working environment.

  • Championing gender equality within the organization and supporting overall staff growth and development.

  • Managing the project budget and project expenditures in compliance with TechnoServe and donor requirements.

  • Ensuring an average return on investment of $3 of income increase at farmer level for every $1 spent on the project.

  • Ensuring the monitoring and evaluation of the project is of suitable quality and that reports are submitted on time.

  • Achieving operational excellence through continuously improving our service delivery to coffee farmers and processors.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Business Administration, Agricultural Economics, or other relevant area with at least 12 years’ experience; OR Master’s Degree + 8 years relevant experience.

  • Project management experience and skills including the ability to effectively manage operations, consistently ensure high quality program execution, and timely donor reporting.

  • Experience managing medium to large teams with excellent people and leadership skills.

  • Experience working within the private sector (eg. F&B industry, Agriculture, Management Consulting etc.) or working on private sector development.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Prior Chief of Staff experience on a US-government funded project and experience working in Ethiopia or East Africa preferable.

  • Experience in the coffee sector preferred

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • Outstanding interpersonal and communication skills. Excellent written and verbal communications including the ability to communicate clearly and effectively to diverse audiences in English.

  • Independent judgment and strong problem-solving and decision-making skills required, with limited supervision.

  • Strong private sector market orientation, entrepreneurial and innovative thinker.

  • Embraces our values of collegiality (we stick our necks out for each other), integrity (doing the ‘right thing’ regardless), resourcefulness (solve problems) and results (bias for action)

We welcome applications from both international and in-country candidates. If the successful candidate is a resident of the operating country, s(he) will be offered a local contract and paid in local currency. Salary for this position is tied to local market rates.

We encourage all qualified individuals who share TechnoServe’s vision of improving the lives of others through proven business solutions to apply.

With our commitment to diversity, we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and affirmative action employer and do not discriminate on the basis of gender, race, color, ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, HIV/AIDS status, protected veteran status, disability and all other protected classes.

We are also proud of our commitment to protecting staff, partners, and beneficiaries from abuse and exploitation and thoroughly vet all final candidates through rigorous background and reference checks.

If you have a disability that affects your ability to use our online system to apply for a position at TechnoServe please contact the Human Resources at recruitment@tns.org or call +1 202 785 4515.

item.title: State Energy Strategy Project Lead at Washington State Department of Commerce
item.description: At the Department of Commerce we’re reimagining what’s possible in government.
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
At the Department of Commerce we’re reimagining what’s possible in government. We’re builders, thinkers, and change-makers, working at the intersection of innovation, community, and impact. From unlocking critical funding to fueling inclusive economic growth, we’re turning big ideas into real-world solutions that uplift people and places.

Our agency’s strength lies in the diversity of our workforce and the breadth of the lived experiences and perspectives employees bring to the work. We believe equity is not just a value but a practice, which is reflected in how we design programs, engage communities, and deliver outcomes. We foster a workplace culture where curiosity is encouraged, bold thinking is welcomed, and collaboration drives our impact.

This job is a commitment to reshape systems so they work better for everyone. If you’re ready to challenge the status quo and build meaningful connections, we want to meet you.

Let’s build what’s next, together.

The Energy Division (Energy) leads Washington’s transition to a clean, affordable, and equitable energy future by providing statewide energy policy leadership, guiding investments, and advancing initiatives that serve all communities.

This position works within the Energy Policy team of the Energy Division. This position is the project lead responsible for supporting the development of the next State Energy Strategy in accordance with RCW 42.21F.088 and RCW 42.21F.090. The State Energy Strategy is published every eight years, delivered to the Governor and the Legislature, and provides Washington’s roadmap for meeting climate and clean energy goals while prioritizing reliability and affordability. It is relied upon by legislators, state agencies, utilities, advocates, and many others as the state’s foundational planning document.

The position will manage the analysis, drafting, public engagement process, advisory committee coordination, and other guidance supporting the final publication of the State Energy Strategy, working with complex datasets across diverse energy topics and collaborating with state executives, subject matter experts, industry sectors, utilities, labor unions, tribal nations, elected officials, interested parties and stakeholders.

View the 2021 Washington State Energy Strategy: Washington State Energy Strategy – Washington State Department of Commerce

This project position is expected to be funded for a minimum duration of 18 months with a possibility of extending to 24 months.

Duties

Production and development of State Energy Strategy report
Tasks include:
• Under the direction of the Assistant Director of Energy Division and the Energy Policy Director, manage the production of the next Washington State Energy Strategy in accordance with RCW 43.21F.088, a document of statewide impact and importance
• Manage key research efforts and conducts analysis of technological developments, state and federal legislation, and regulations. This will include managing and overseeing the work of a contracted energy modeling firm.
• Lead collaboration with diverse groups including state agency representatives, subject matter experts, contracted consultants, utilities, and others to support research and analytical efforts. This may include coordination with other state agencies and programs to compile, review and incorporate data regarding progress from 2021 findings and recommendations.
• Establish and oversee process and methodology for complex data collection and performance analytics, in support of SES initiatives and overall program coordination.
• Consult with diverse groups of executive management, interagency representatives, and subject matter experts to develop metrics, analysis and reporting tools.
• Coordinate with agency teams and leaders as part of report review and finalization process, including ensuring communications and accessibility standards and review deadlines are met.
• Develop recommendations to ensure that tribes, rural communities and low-income households are partners and benefactors in our state’s clean energy transition.

State Energy Strategy Advisory Committee and public involvement processes
Tasks include:
• Facilitate 25-person State Energy Strategy Advisory Committee in accordance with RCW 43.21F.090, and any technical advisory groups.
• Develop, lead and implement public involvement and tribal engagement process including briefings, hearings, public comment periods, and other engagement forums.
• Coordinate with Office of Tribal Relations, engagement teams, and others to develop and implement plans to solicit additional feedback on report development and content.
• Develop and implement outreach to involve young people and youth-led organizations in the development of report content and outreach plans and activities.

Dissemination of findings and next steps for use of report recommendations
Tasks include:
• Oversee the production of communications resources to be used in dissemination of findings, including data visualizations and dashboards, to effectively communicate results to senior leadership, policy makers, and the public. This may involve coordinating with and overseeing work of contractors as well as working with Commerce communications teams.
• Present research findings, recommendations and draft report to executive level decision-makers, elected officials, and others in a variety of formats and settings.
• Provide recommendations regarding how to communicate research results and findings
• Collaborate with Energy Division and agency legislative staff regarding dissemination of key findings to legislators and/or use of findings to inform legislative development.

Qualifications

Required Position Qualifications:
Five (5) years of combined experience and/or education as described below:
Experience must include:
A minimum of five years of technical experience in two or more of the following areas:
• Conducting research
• Analyzing policies, laws, rules, or regulations
• Leading large, multi-stakeholder processes and projects
• Analyzing and using complex data sets of varied sources and wide-ranging topics
• Writing and/or presenting concise analytical findings using compelling graphical and narrative communication
• Experience with statistical analysis, performance assessment, and results measures.
• Experience developing data management strategies, processes, and tools.
• Experience creating dashboards and interactive tools to display data and results.
• Ability to analyze and interpret data, perform trend analysis, and communicate conclusions.
• Skill in presenting data in a variety of ways to best display the meaning and implications of the data.
• Ability to engage diverse stakeholders and translate input into recommendations
• Knowledge of state agency processes including policy development and planning or similar processes.
• Ability to communicate clearly with diverse groups, including senior level management, elected officials, subject matter experts, and other interested parties.
• Intermediate skill level for MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint, Visio, and database software.
• Ability to connect detailed analyses to big picture strategy
• Excellent time management, ability to work independently

Education involves energy policy, public policy, environmental science, business administration or related field. Qualifying education post High School or equivalent may be substituted year for year for experience.
